title: Morphisms from a shifted free DG module in the DG derived category
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. For $k\in\mathbf Z$ let $A[k]$ be the shifted module with $A[k]^i=A^{i+k}$, differential $d_{A[k]}=(-1)^kd_A$ and right action by multiplication, so that the unit $1\in A^0$ lies in $A[k]^{-k}$. Let $M$ be a right differential graded $A$-module. Every morphism $A[k]\to M$ in $D(A,d)$ is the image of a homomorphism $f:A[k]\to M$ of differential graded modules (degree-preserving, $A$-linear, commuting with the differentials), and $f\mapsto[f(1)]$ induces an additive bijection $$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(A[k],M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^{-k}(M)=\ker(d:M^{-k}\to M^{-k+1})/d(M^{-k-1}).$$ In particular two such homomorphisms $f,g$ have the same image in $D(A,d)$ if and only if $f(1)-g(1)$ is a boundary. The bijection is natural in $M$: for a homomorphism $h:M\to M'$ of differential graded modules, composition with the image of $h$ corresponds to $H^{-k}(h)$. No boundedness, countability or flatness hypothesis on $A$ or $M$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the mapping complex of [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived]. For any right DG module $N$, evaluation at $1$ identifies its degree-$r$ group $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[k],N)^r$ with $N^{r-k}$: the inverse sends $x$ to $f_x(a)=xa$. The unit satisfies $d_A1=d_A(1\cdot1)=2d_A1$, hence $d_A1=0$, so evaluation sends $\partial f=d_Nf-(-1)^rf d_{A[k]}$ to $d_N(f(1))$. Explicitly, the terms involving $d_Aa$ cancel since $(-1)^{r-k}=(-1)^{r+k}$. Thus this is an additive identification of the complexes with terms $N^{r-k}$ and differential $d_N$.

With $N=M$, closed degree-zero maps in Step 1 are precisely the DG module maps $A[k]\to M$, corresponding to cycles in $M^{-k}$. Degree-zero boundaries are homotopies: if $f(1)-g(1)=d_My$ for $y\in M^{-k-1}$, the degree-$-1$ map $s(a)=ya$ satisfies $f-g=d_Ms+s d_{A[k]}$. Conversely every such homotopy gives that boundary on evaluation at $1$. The definition $\operatorname{Hom}_K=H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}$ in [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived] therefore gives the additive bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(A[k],M)\cong H^{-k}(M)$.

For acyclic $N$, the complex calculated in Step 1 is acyclic in every degree, since its degree-$r$ cohomology is $H^{r-k}(N)=0$. Hence $A[k]$ is homotopically projective in the precise sense of [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived]. That theorem makes the canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(A[k],M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(A[k],M)$ bijective. Combine its inverse with Step 2. Every homotopy class has a DG map representative, so every derived morphism has one; injectivity gives exactly the asserted boundary criterion. Addition is preserved: sums in the additive localization are represented by sums of these maps, and $(f+g)(1)=f(1)+g(1)$.

source.place: Tag 09KY, lemma-hom-derived (1), proof, using the acyclic-target vanishing of Tag 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective.

proof.text: For a DG module map $h:M\to M^{\prime}$, a representative $f$ is sent to $hf$, and $(hf)(1)=h(f(1))$. Since $h$ preserves cycles and boundaries, this induces $[h(f(1))]=H^{-k}(h)([f(1)])$. This proves the required naturality. All arguments allow arbitrary integers $k$, unbounded modules, and arbitrary underlying cardinalities; none uses flatness.
